case_title: Narender Singh & Ors. v. State of Madhya Pradesh
accused_victim_relationship: Prior enmity/dispute (old enmity recorded in the FIR crime details form; this is the prosecution's recorded motive, not a finding on the relationship)
statutory_provisions: IPC s.302 r/w ss.148 and 149 (conviction); charged also under IPC ss.147 and 294
evidence_type: Eyewitness (injured eyewitness and corroborating eyewitnesses); medical evidence (MLC and post mortem); documentary records (FIR, crime details form, express report); recovery of weapons; Section 27 disclosure statements
confession: Section 27 disclosure statements (Exhibits P18-P21) were relied on as supporting the investigation; they are not described as a confession by any accused
aggravating_circumstances: Group attack with sharp weapons and lathis; eight injuries on the deceased, four grievous; the crime details form records intention to kill
trial_court_outcome: Convicted under IPC s.302 r/w ss.148 and 149; sentenced to life imprisonment
high_court_outcome: Appeal (Criminal Appeal No. 666 of 2000) dismissed; conviction and life sentence confirmed
offence_finally_established: Murder under IPC s.302 r/w ss.148 and 149
neutral_facts: On the night of 27 June 1997, around 10:00 p.m., the victim, who was a village sarpanch, was sitting and talking with two other persons near a hotel in the village, with street lights on and a chimney burning nearby. Several men arrived at the spot. One carried a sword, another a farsa, another an axe, and the rest lathis. The man with the sword, while abusing the victim and saying he could not escape that day, struck the victim on the head, causing bleeding. Another assailant then struck the victim's head with the farsa, and a third struck the head with an axe, after which the victim fell. Others struck with lathis. Witnesses pleaded for the victim to be spared, and the assailants left after warning the victim not to contest against them in future. The injured eyewitness went to the police station about one kilometre away, and a first information report was registered at 10:45 p.m. The investigating officer visited the scene at 11:10 p.m. and prepared the crime details form. The injured eyewitness was sent for medical examination, completed by 1:30 a.m. The post mortem recorded eight injuries on the body, four of them grievous. The body was taken to the hospital by 7:30 a.m. the next day. Witnesses who came on hearing shouts corroborated the account. The accused were arrested on 28 June 1997, weapons were seized on 29 June 1997 at their instance, and disclosure statements were recorded. The express report was received by the magistrate only on 30 June 1997.
physical_harm: Death of the deceased from head and body injuries (eight injuries, four grievous, from sword, farsa, axe and lathis); the injured eyewitness also sustained injuries
motive: alleged: old enmity (as recorded in the crime details form); the court did not separately decide the motive
key_evidence_accepted: Eyewitness testimony of injured P.W.3 and P.W.6, corroborated by P.Ws. 7 and 11; MLC of P.W.3 (Exhibit P1) and Exhibits P1A and P1B; post mortem evidence of P.W.10; weapons recovered at the appellants' instance; arrest and seizure records; crime details form and contemporaneous FIR documents
witness_credibility: P.W.3 (injured eyewitness) found cogent in every respect; his presence and injuries held established by the doctor's evidence; P.W.6 supportive; P.W.10's evidence found to fully support the prosecution; the court relied on the Bhajan Singh principle that an injured witness's testimony is accorded special status
post_offence_conduct: Arrested on 28 June 1997; weapons recovered at their instance on 29 June 1997; the accused left the place of occurrence after warning the victim
trial_duration: offence: 27 June 1997; trial judgment: not given; High Court: 7 September 2006; Supreme Court: 29 September 2015
legal_representation: Appellants: Tripurari Ray, Dhirendra Singh Parmar, Suresh Kumar Sharma, Rajinder Singh, Susheel Tomar, Ms. Abha R. Sharma (Advocates). State: Arjun Garg, Manish Yadav, Mishra Saurabh (Advocates)
investigation_status: FIR registered at 10:45 p.m. on 27 June 1997; investigating officer visited scene; medical examination and post mortem conducted; arrests 28 June 1997; seizures 29 June 1997; charge sheet filed; trial completed
procedural_irregularity: Delay in forwarding the Express Report under s.157 CrPC to the Illaka Magistrate (received 1:20 p.m. on 30 June 1997); the court held it caused no serious prejudice
appeal_history: Trial court: convicted under s.302 r/w ss.148 and 149 IPC, life imprisonment. High Court: appeal dismissed, conviction and sentence confirmed. Supreme Court: appeals dismissed
prosecution_argument: Arrest, seizure and Section 27 statements established involvement; the delay in the Express Report caused no prejudice; eyewitness account and medical evidence were clinching; the FIR was registered in time and the Express Report was sent through a constable on 27 June 1997
defence_argument: FIR was ante-dated; injured witness P.W.3's injuries were fake and his presence doubtful; eyewitness Ranganath Sharma was not examined; unexplained delay in forwarding the Express Report; omissions in the crime details form and other documents; weapons not linked to the injuries; minor infirmities
legal_principle_applied: Delay in sending the report to the Magistrate is not fatal unless prejudice is shown; evidence of an injured eyewitness is accorded special status; contemporaneous documents and other corroborating evidence can cure non-mention in a statutory form; minor discrepancies do not impinge on the judgment
precedent_relied_upon: Pala Singh v. State of Punjab (1972) 2 SCC 640; State of Karnataka v. Main Patel (1996) 8 SCC 167; Bhajan Singh @ Harbhajan Singh v. State of Haryana (2011) 7 SCC 421
